lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Education appears before the more relevant Experience section.
items.because: A reader may reach the work and project evidence later than necessary.

items.says: The 35% accuracy improvement lacks a measurement basis.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it is a relative gain or percentage-point increase, or what it is compared against.

items.says: The disagreement reduction comes after the routing-layer description.
items.because: The technical setup makes the result harder to spot while scanning.

items.says: The calls and latency reductions come after a long methods phrase.
items.because: The technical setup makes the results harder to spot while scanning.

items.says: “The team used to compare” is indirect phrasing.
items.because: It lengthens the sentence without clarifying the harness’s role.

items.says: The assistant-only-loss-masking adapter work repeats the first internship bullet without showing a distinct achievement.
items.because: The first bullet already reports the accuracy improvement from fine-tuning the adapter.

items.says: The FP32-to-BF16 switch does not by itself support a fourfold reduction in total GPU memory.
items.because: BF16 uses about half the storage per converted value, mixed precision may retain FP32 state, and the measurement conditions are missing.

items.says: The load-test evidence comes after the latency result and implementation details.
items.because: Its placement makes the validation easier to miss while scanning.

items.says: The CI bullet switches from past-tense “Maintained” to present-tense “adds.”
items.because: The role ended in July 2024, so the tense shift makes the timing unclear.

items.says: “Maintained the CI pipeline” names an ongoing duty rather than the specific change made.
The three-day release-cycle figure lacks a defined measure and prior comparison.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it means cycle duration or release cadence, or how much either changed.

items.says: The release-cycle result comes after the CI methods.
items.because: The clearest measure of impact is less visible when scanning.

items.says: The migration is credited with clearing nightly backlogs without evidence that queued work could finish before dispatch.
items.because: A queue does not itself increase processing capacity, and retries can add work.

items.says: The backlog and dispatch-delay change has no before-and-after measure.
items.because: The count of migrated services shows scope, not the scale of the operational effect.

items.says: “AI-first engineering practices” does not identify the practice adopted.
items.because: The reader cannot see what changed or what supported the adoption claim.

items.says: The broad adoption claim reads as a separate item beside the concrete runtime improvements.
items.because: Its general benefits lack a checkable result and make the project’s technical focus less clear.

items.says: The under-10K-token claim does not define working context or show that complete model input stayed below the threshold.
items.because: Retained conversation state could omit instructions, tool content, summaries, or an oversized turn.

items.says: The 100x conversation-growth figure lacks a starting point.
items.because: The reader cannot interpret the scale of the stress test or what the growth represents.

items.says: The two runtime changes are said to have removed deadlocks and lost results without establishing that outcome.
items.because: Pool separation and stream completion do not rule out the stated failures.

items.says: The 50-way test condition has no validation measure for the claimed removal of failures.
items.because: The reader cannot see what evidence established that the failures were removed.

items.says: The two fixes come before the result.
items.because: A reader must reach the end of the bullet to see the claimed impact.

items.says: The metrics bullet does not say what the integration changed for the framework or its users.
items.because: Without an enabled capability or user outcome, its value beyond the technical deliverable is hard to judge.

items.says: The 0.89 Kendall correlation does not on its own establish that the evaluator tracks degradation, and its comparator is unnamed.
items.because: The degradation order, score direction, ties, repeated variants, and possible differences across reports or removal types affect what it demonstrates.

items.says: The correlation result should lead, with a shorter trailing explanation.
The same backlog-reduction achievement appears under two entries with slightly different figures.
items.because: Both describe a triage branch screening 800+ signals, while 68% and two-thirds leave the reported figure uncertain.

items.says: The triage-method clause is dense after the backlog result.
items.because: Its technical details slow the reader and make the main point harder to scan.

items.says: The adapter fine-tuning work does not establish that LoRA was used.
items.because: The experience bullets do not identify LoRA, leaving no example to support its place in the skills list.
